title: One object
rule: Only one 3D object on the page. Every section must be about it.

title: No hero headline
rule: The object is the headline. Text starts only after the first scroll.

title: Thumb only
rule: Design the phone first. Every interaction must work with one thumb in the bottom 40% of the screen.

title: Three colours
rule: Exactly three colours: paper, ink, one accent used at about 1%.

title: One verb
rule: The whole page is one verb (pour, fold, wind, open). Every interaction is that verb.

title: Real scale
rule: Show the object at real size somewhere (a ruler, a hand-width, a coin).

title: Sound off
rule: The page must make sense with no sound and no hover.

title: Ten seconds
rule: A visitor must understand the brand in ten seconds without reading.

title: Cut a section
rule: Write the page, then delete the weakest section. Nothing else is allowed to grow to fill it.

title: Wrong category
rule: Borrow the layout of a totally different category (a museum label for a barber, a train timetable for a bakery).

title: Macro first
rule: Open on an extreme close-up of the material; pull back only on scroll.

title: One camera move
rule: The whole 3D scene uses one continuous camera move. No cuts.

title: Data as decoration
rule: Every decorative element is a real number about the product (weight, temperature, minutes).

title: Night mode is the story
rule: The light switch is not a setting, it is the plot.

title: No cards
rule: No card grids anywhere. Lists, tables, rails, drawers or a single column only.

title: Hand-made detail x3
rule: Name three details a template would never have before you write code.

title: Credit visible
rule: Every outside asset is credited on screen, and the credit looks designed, not hidden.

title: Phone = PC
rule: The phone build loads the same model, textures and lighting. Plan the composition so nothing has to be cut.

title: Slow down
rule: Every motion is 400-700 ms, expo-out, no bounce. If it needs bounce to be fun, the idea is weak.

title: Honest form
rule: The form must tell the truth: 'Concept: not sent'.
